note: Also the auxiliary for many verbs in the passato prossimo: *sono arrivato*, *è partita*. Its passato *sono stato* is also the passato of *stare*: it means both *I was / have been* and *I stayed*.

Used for how you are (*Come stai? Sto bene.*) and with the gerund for what is happening right now: *sto mangiando* = I am eating. Its passato *sono stato* is the same as that of *essere*: *sono stato a casa* = I stayed / was at home.
Also the auxiliary for most verbs in the passato prossimo: *ho mangiato*.
No imperativo. With another verb, the passato prossimo often takes that verb's auxiliary: *non sono potuto venire*.
*Vorrei* = I would like: the polite way to ask for something. No imperativo in everyday use.

en_presente: have to;have to;has to;have to;have to;have to
note: *Dovrei* = I should. No imperativo. With another verb, the passato prossimo often takes that verb's auxiliary: *sono dovuto partire*.

english: to know (facts), to know how to
note: For facts and skills (*so nuotare* = I can swim); for people and places use *conoscere*. In the passato prossimo it usually means *found out*: *l'ho saputo ieri*.
